chunks: If a woman leaves behind her husband, her father, and brothers and sisters from both parents, or from the father, or from the mother, then the husband has one-half, and what remains belongs to the father. The brothers and sisters have nothing alongside the father, nor alongside the mother.

Likewise, if she leaves behind her husband, her mother, and brothers and sisters from both parents, or from the father, or from the mother, then the husband has one-half, the mother has one-sixth, and what remains is returned to her. The brothers and sisters all fall away, because the mother possesses a fixed share, and she is the nearest of the blood relatives; she is related in her own right, while the siblings are related through others.
If she leaves behind a husband, a mother, maternal siblings, and a sister from both parents, then the husband has one-half, and what remains belongs to the mother.

If she leaves behind her husband, her two parents, and siblings from both parents or from the father, then the husband has one-half, the mother has one-sixth, and the father has the remainder. But if the siblings are from the mother, then the husband has one-half, the mother has one-third, and the father has one-sixth.

key_terms.أَقْرَبُ ٱلْأَرْحَامِ: The nearer blood relative who takes precedence in inheritance.
key_terms.ذَاتُ سَهْمٍ: A relative who possesses a fixed assigned share in inheritance.
key_terms.رُدَّ عَلَيْهَا: The remainder of the estate is returned to her after fixed shares.
key_terms.سَقَطَ ٱلْإِخْوَةُ وَٱلْأَخَوَاتُ: The brothers and sisters are excluded from inheriting.
key_terms.ٱلثُّلُثُ: One-third of the estate as a prescribed share.
key_terms.ٱلسُّدُسُ: One-sixth of the estate as a prescribed share.
key_terms.ٱلنِّصْفُ: One-half of the estate as a fixed inheritance share.

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided in Shia fiqh when a woman dies leaving a husband, parents, and siblings?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for inheritance when a woman dies leaving a husband, parents, and various categories of siblings. It explains the fixed shares of the husband and mother, the priority of the father and mother over siblings, and when siblings are excluded from inheritance altogether.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: If a woman dies and leaves behind her husband, her father, and siblings (whether they are from both parents, the father's side, or the mother's side), the husband receives half of the inheritance, and the remainder goes to the father. The siblings, whether brothers or sisters, inherit nothing alongside the father or the mother.

Similarly, if she leaves behind her husband, her mother, and siblings (whether they are from both parents, the father's side, or the mother's side), the husband receives half of the inheritance, the mother receives one-sixth, and the remainder is returned to the mother. The siblings are entirely excluded because the mother holds a fixed share and is the closest relative by direct lineage, whereas the siblings are related indirectly.
If she leaves behind her husband, her mother, maternal siblings, and a sister from both parents, the husband receives half of the inheritance, and the remainder goes to the mother.

If she leaves behind her husband, both parents, and siblings from both parents or from the father's side, the husband receives half, the mother receives one-sixth, and the remainder goes to the father. However, if the siblings are solely from the mother's side, the husband receives half, the mother receives one-third, and the father receives one-sixth.
